key_insight: OmegaUse-OfficeVal introduces a benchmark for testing whether LLM agents can complete long-horizon office-suite tasks while staying economically sensible. It goes beyond simple task success by grounding evaluation in task-level cost and effort.
problem_solved: Existing LLM agent benchmarks often measure completion accuracy but fail to assess whether agents can handle realistic office workflows at a reasonable cost. This paper addresses the need for an evaluation framework that reflects both long-term task execution and economic practicality.
method: Built a benchmark of 100 office-suite tasks derived from practitioner requests and adapted into evaluation-ready scenarios.
Focuses on long-horizon workflows that require multiple steps across office applications rather than isolated actions.
Adds task-level economic grounding so agents are evaluated not only on success, but also on the cost of completing each task.
impact: This benchmark helps researchers and practitioners understand which LLM agents are truly useful for real office work, not just technically capable. It can guide the development of more efficient, reliable, and cost-aware agent systems.

paper_title: OmegaUse-OfficeVal: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Office-Suite Tasks with Economic Grounding
paper_authors: Jingbo Zhou, Yusai Zhao, Qi Bao, Jingjia Cao, Zhenghai Chen
